plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. Widely cultivated in gardens and commercial fields, it attracts bees and butterflies and is prized for its essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, typically June through August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large composite flower head made of hundreds of tiny florets. The heads track the sun during early growth and produce edible seeds and oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn, peaking in late July and August
plants.location: Native to North America; grown across the United States, Ukraine, Russia, France, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west in a behavior called heliotropism, but mature blooms stay facing east.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular flowers on tall stalks. It thrives in warm shallow ponds and wetlands and is culturally significant across Asia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, with peak bloom from July to August
plants.location: Native to Asia and northern Australia; cultivated in India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and Thailand
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a micro-textured surface that repels water and dirt, known as the 'lotus effect', which inspired self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.description: A rugged Australian tree or shrub with gnarled bark and large cylindrical flower spikes made of thousands of tiny flowers. It is an important nectar source for birds, bats, and insects during the southern winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to winter, with flowers present in the Southern Hemisphere winter around July and August
plants.location: Eastern Australia, from Queensland to Victoria and Tasmania, in coastal heath and woodland
plants.funFact: Banksia seed cones are woody and often only release their seeds after bushfires, making them well adapted to fire-prone landscapes.
